proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local reconstruction, not a source transcription. Positivity and Cauchy-Schwarz give ||Ay||>=m||y||, so A has closed range and trivial kernel. Self-adjointness implies range(A)^perp=ker(A)=0, hence its closed range is H. Thus x*=A^{-1}b exists uniquely. Expansion gives f(x)-f(x*)=<A(x-x*),x-x*>/2>=m||x-x*||^2/2, proving unique minimization. Subtract Ax*=b from the update to obtain e_{n+1}=((1+q^2)I-alpha A)e_n-q^2 e_{n-1}. Its scalar characteristic polynomial is z^2-(1+beta-alpha lambda)z+beta; the printed -beta on p14 is not used. If m<M then q>0. Set T=((1+q^2)I-alpha A)/(2q). Substitution gives t(m)=1 and t(M)=-1 for t(lambda)=(1+q^2-alpha lambda)/(2q). The standard spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators therefore gives spectrum(T) contained in [-1,1] and ||p(T)||<=sup_{[-1,1]}|p| for every real polynomial p. Define U_{-1}=0, U_0=1, U_{k+1}(t)=2tU_k(t)-U_{k-1}(t). For t=cos(theta), this recurrence gives U_k(cos(theta))=sum_{j=0}^k exp(i(k-2j)theta): the formula holds for k=0,1 and multiplication by 2cos(theta), followed by subtraction of the preceding sum, proves the induction step. Thus |U_k(t)|<=k+1 on [-1,1], including endpoints by continuity. Induction in the error recurrence yields e_n=q^{n-1}U_{n-1}(T)e1-q^n U_{n-2}(T)e0 for n>=1: n=1 uses U_{-1}=0, n=2 is the update, and subsequent steps use the U recurrence. Consequently ||e_n||<=nq^{n-1}||e1||+(n-1)q^n||e0||<=R[nq^{n-1}+(n-1)q^n]. Put a=q+epsilon and r=q/a. Division by a^n bounds the bracket by (q^{-1}+1)nr^n. Since 0<r<1, each nr^n is at most sum_{j>=1}jr^j=r/(1-r)^2. The stated C therefore works for n>=1, and C>=1 covers n=0. Since a<1, convergence follows. If m=M, the self-adjoint operator A-mI has zero quadratic form everywhere, so polarization gives A=mI. Then q=beta=0 and alpha=1/m, hence e_{n+1}=0 for n>=1. For n=0,1 use ||e_i||<=R and C=max(1,epsilon^{-1}); all later errors vanish. This proves the boundary case. The foundational tool invoked is the standard bounded self-adjoint spectral theorem and its polynomial norm inequality; no unreviewed Memory lead is used as mathematical evidence.

assumptions: 0<m<=M<infinity and m||y||^2<=<Ay,y><=M||y||^2 for every y in H.
x0,x1 are arbitrary points in H. For every integer n>=1 use x_{n+1}=x_n-alpha(Ax_n-b)+beta(x_n-x_{n-1}).
alpha=4/(sqrt(M)+sqrt(m))^2 and beta=q^2; exact arithmetic recurrence with no gradient error, projection or changing parameters.
statement.conclusion: The unique minimizer x* exists and ||x_n-x*||<=C(q,epsilon)R(q+epsilon)^n, hence x_n converges to x*. For q>0 one admissible local-proof constant is C=1+(q^{-1}+1)r/(1-r)^2, r=q/(q+epsilon). For q=0, A=mI and x_n=x* for n>=2; C=max(1,epsilon^{-1}) suffices. These explicit constants are locally supplied, not attributed to the paper.
statement.objects_and_definitions: H is a real Hilbert space. A:H->H is bounded self-adjoint, b in H, c real, and f(x)=<x,Ax>/2-<b,x>+c. Define x*=A^{-1}b, e_n=x_n-x*, R=(||e0||^2+||e1||^2)^{1/2}, and q=(sqrt(M)-sqrt(m))/(sqrt(M)+sqrt(m)).
statement.parameter_domains: 0<m<=M<infinity; q in [0,1); epsilon in (0,1-q); integer n>=0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible H,A,b,c,m,M and every epsilon in (0,1-q), a finite C(q,epsilon) exists, independent of n, initial points, b and dimension, such that the conclusion holds for every x0,x1 and every integer n>=0. Everything is deterministic.
